title: Calico durable capture attempt (v2)
description: Closed additive successor to the two existing timing-less v1 attempt shapes written by calico_landing.admission and calico_landing.store (04-04-PLAN.md D-02/D-12/D-13). Records one true attempt identity plus actual UTC start/end captured once at the admit() boundary; carries only nullable structural release-identity/reason fields sufficient to distinguish accepted, no_new_release, rejected, and recovered outcomes. Performs no outcome normalization, duration calculation, or analytical classification -- that work belongs exclusively to dbt/models/intermediate/int_capture_runs.sql. Existing v1 admission-level and store-level documents are never rewritten to this shape; both remain readable through calico_landing.attempts with permanently unavailable timing.

attempt_id.description: One durable attempt identity captured once at the admit() boundary -- never inferred from a filename, UUID content beyond its own generation, or any other source.

started_at_utc.description: Timezone-aware actual UTC timestamp captured once when admit() begins.

ended_at_utc.description: Timezone-aware actual UTC timestamp captured once after the decided structural outcome.

status.description: Closed structural outcome vocabulary. 'recovered' distinguishes a commit that completed an earlier crashed process's unfinished promotion from an ordinary fresh 'accepted' commit; SQL, not this field, decides what either means analytically.

as_of_date.description: Best-effort source as-of date, or null when no candidate date could be structurally determined (e.g. a candidate-boundary rejection before any row was parsed).

release_revision.description: The committed release revision number, present only for accepted/no_new_release/recovered outcomes.

revision_fingerprint.description: The committed revision's ordered-source-hash fingerprint, present only for accepted/no_new_release/recovered outcomes.

reason_count.description: The number of structural admission-rejection reasons, present only for the rejected outcome; never the reasons themselves.
